title: Closed-subset sections extend to a neighborhood
statement: Let $X$ be a paracompact Hausdorff topological space, where paracompact means that every open cover admits a locally finite open refinement. Let $G$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on its open-subset site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $S\subseteq X$ be closed, and let $i:S\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion with the subspace topology. Write $G|_S=i^{-1}G$ for the inverse-image sheaf: a section on $S$ is a family of germs in $G_x$, locally represented on $S$ by sections of $G$ on open subsets of $X$. For every $s\in\Gamma(S,G|_S)$ there exist an open neighborhood $U\supseteq S$ in $X$ and $t\in G(U)$ whose restriction to $S$ is $s$.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf. IV §4, Lemma (4.6)(a), Theorem (4.7), Corollary (4.8), printed pp.203--204. The printed occurrence of a neighborhood of A in (4.7) means a neighborhood of S.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, take $U=X$ and $t=0$. Otherwise, by the stated local-representative description of $i^{-1}G$, choose for each $a\in S$ an open $U_a\ni a$ and $s_a\in G(U_a)$ whose germ at every $x\in S\cap U_a$ is $s(x)$. Thus $(U_a)_{a\in S}$ covers $S$. Recall explicitly that two germs represented by sections are equal exactly when the sections agree after restriction to some common open neighborhood of the point.

source.place: IV §4, Theorem (4.7), proof, printed pp.203--204; Corollary (4.8). Germ convention: Stacks, sheaves.tex, Section 0078 (section-stalks), the equivalence relation defining a stalk.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-paracompact-closed-cover-refinement] to this cover of the closed set $S$. Obtain open $W_a\subseteq U_a$ covering $S$, locally finite in all of $X$.

source.place: IV §4.B, Definition (4.5), Lemma (4.6)(a), printed p.203; precise_refinement_set in Mathlib.

proof.text: For $x\in S$, an open neighborhood meeting only finitely many $W_a$ shows that only finitely many $W_a$ contain $x$. Apply [lem-sfb-paracompact-point-finite-shrinking] to get open $V_a$ covering $S$ with $\overline{V_a}\subseteq W_a\subseteq U_a$. Since $V_a\subseteq W_a$, the same neighborhoods show that $(V_a)$ is locally finite in $X$.

source.place: IV §4.B, shrinking discussion, Definition (4.5), Lemma (4.6)(a), printed p.203; exists_subset_iUnion_closure_subset in Mathlib.

proof.text: Put $O=\bigcup_a V_a$ and $E=\{x\in O:(s_a)_x=(s_b)_x\text{ whenever }x\in\overline{V_a}\cap\overline{V_b}\}$. The germs in this formula are defined because $\overline{V_a}\subseteq U_a$. For $x\in S$, both germs in each required equality are $s(x)$, so $S\subseteq E$.

source.place: IV §4, Theorem (4.7), proof, printed pp.203--204; Corollary (4.8).

proof.text:
The set $E$ is open. Fix $p\in E$ and choose an open neighborhood $N$ meeting only finitely many $V_a$; write $J$ for those indices. If $a
otin J$, the open set $N$ also misses $\overline{V_a}$, by the definition of closure. Remove from $N$ the finitely many closed sets $\overline{V_a}$ for $a\in J$ with $p
otin\overline{V_a}$. The resulting open neighborhood $N_0$ meets only closures indexed by $L=\{a\in J:p\in\overline{V_a}\}$. For each of the finitely many pairs $a,b\in L$, membership $p\in E$ and the germ equivalence relation give an open $N_{ab}
i p$ inside $U_a\cap U_b$ on which $s_a$ and $s_b$ agree. Intersect $N_0$, $O$, and all $N_{ab}$. This is an open neighborhood of $p$ contained in $E$: any pair of closures through a point of this intersection has indices in $L$, and the corresponding sections agree there. Thus $E$ is an open neighborhood of $S$. The locally finite family and its closure containment are exactly those supplied by [lem-sfb-paracompact-closed-cover-refinement] and [lem-sfb-paracompact-point-finite-shrinking]; the argument uses only finite intersections, not compactness of $S$.

source.place: IV §4, Theorem (4.7), proof, printed pp.203--204; Corollary (4.8).

proof.text: On the open cover $(E\cap V_a)_a$ of $E$, restrict $s_a$. On a pairwise intersection, their germs agree at every point by the definition of $E$, hence the sections agree by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs], applied to the underlying sheaf of sets. The sheaf equalizer axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) now glues them to $t\in G(E)$. For $x\in S$, choose $a$ with $x\in V_a$; then $t_x=(s_a)_x=s(x)$. In the specified family-of-germs description of $i^{-1}G$, this says exactly $t|_S=s$. Take $U=E$.

source.place: IV §4, Theorem (4.7), proof, printed pp.203--204; Corollary (4.8).
